title: Case F — Shinjuku district
summary: Shinjuku sub-centre, Tokyo, November 1978: 1:800 tunnel (thermistor, 5 / 9 / 20 m) and a year of field cup anemometers; velocity ratio to the 500 m wind, 12 tunnel and 16 field directions.

configuration.district: Shinjuku sub-centre during construction of the high-rise group, building configuration of November 1978
configuration.model: terrain and buildings in a disc of radius 725 m (BD_caseF.stl; the readme and the data paper say 800 m / 1600 m diameter)
configuration.point_numbers: 1-3, 5-11, 13-15 (4 and 12 absent; points 16 and later belong to later construction stages and are not in the dataset)
configuration.normalisation: velocity ratio = mean speed / the approaching mean speed at the boundary-layer height 500 m (full scale); the field values were converted to it with the tunnel (readme). U(500 m) is 10 m/s in the data paper and 10.65 m/s implied by the profile
configuration.instrument: tunnel: thermistor anemometer, 30 s averaging; field: three-cup anemometer with wind vane, 10-minute means above 5 m/s at the reference roof, December 1977 - November 1978
configuration.tunnel: Shimizu Corporation wind tunnel; cross-section 1.55 m wide, 2.2 m high; power-law inflow, exponent 1/4

reference_roofs.SMB: Shinjuku-Mitsui Building, roof G.L.+210 m, anemometer G.L.+237 m, for NW-NE
reference_roofs.KDD: KDD Building, roof G.L.+165 m, anemometer G.L.+187 m, for the other directions

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced district, tunnel floor plane
frame.z: +z up from the TUNNEL FLOOR; the readme's rule is ground = z - 10 m (the STL's terrain under the points is at z = 5 m)
frame.wind_direction_rotation: compass FROM-direction (N = 0, E = 90), so N blows toward -y; flow_dir = (-sin WD, -cos WD). Not stated by the sources; supported by the reference-building choice and by upwind roughness, and at NNW by a solved field (status 'corroborated by a solved field'; the other directions stay 'unverified').

inflow_fit.method: power law on the 18 published heights (z 10 ... 400 m full scale); the data paper states exponent 1/4
inflow_fit.note: AF_caseF.csv stops at 400 m (U = 10.0 m/s); the workbook's U/UR profile (0.94 at 400 m) puts the 500 m speed at 10.65 m/s

fit.method: power law on the 18 published heights (z 10 ... 400 m full scale); the data paper states exponent 1/4
fit.note: AF_caseF.csv stops at 400 m (U = 10.0 m/s); the workbook's U/UR profile (0.94 at 400 m) puts the 500 m speed at 10.65 m/s

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): no log law fits this case (inflow_fit says why); use the measured approach-flow profile as a tabulated inlet (approach_flow.csv). Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) and, where published, k(z) tabulated from approach_flow.csv; epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz where k is published, else from your own closure
recommended.openfoam: fixedProfile (OpenFOAM.org) with the table, or timeVaryingMappedFixedValue: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds the table

flow_direction.meaning: meteorological FROM-direction theta, clockwise from north: flowDir (-sin theta, -cos theta, 0)

eddy3d_runs.inlet: manual (the workbook's Inflow sheet, ZR 500 m, UR 10 m/s, 20 rows)
manual (the workbook's Inflow sheet, ZR 500 m, UR 10 m/s, 20 rows)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: the table holds the mean speed over U(500 m); give ratios over your own U(500 m) of the approach flow

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: uv run python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (pyproject.toml)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: The 16 field rows of point 14 in RS-FO_caseF.csv hold the workbook's value of the NEXT wind direction clockwise (the series is shifted by one); the cleaned table follows the workbook (clean/QUESTIONS.md QF1).
Tunnel and STL coordinates are MODEL scale (1:800); the field's are full scale. The case frame is full scale; the tunnel's x, y, z and the STL are multiplied by 800.

z is height above the tunnel floor. The readme's rule 'ground = z - 10 m' gives the 5 / 9 / 20 m planes, but the STL's terrain under all 13 points is at z = 5 m, so the planes stand 10 / 14 / 25 m above it.

BD_caseF.stl is wound inward on every ground, roof and sampled wall facet and is open along the rim of its 725 m disc (812 boundary edges); the served geometry.stl is re-wound outward and closed with a base slab down to z = -1 m.

MP_caseF.csv names the two reference points the other way round from the workbook, the STL and MP_caseF.png (the workbook's Shinjuku-Mitsui Building is the 225 m tower at (-17.5, 96.0), the KDD Building the 180 m one at (85.8, -347.1)).

Field values are the legacy workbook's roof-anemometer ratios times 0.940 (NW-NE) or 0.963 (other directions); sigma is the workbook's S.D. rounded to 0.01 times that factor, so it moves in steps of 0.0094 / 0.0096.
The tunnel did not run E, ESE, WSW or W; the field data cover all 16. The 5 m and 20 m planes exist at some points only (29 and 79 rows).
One tunnel value (point 8, SW, 9 m: 0.474) has no counterpart in the workbook's results sheet, and the flat 'Sheet1' table has 0.63 there.
Field anemometer heights above the tunnel floor are 13 - 21 m (3 - 11 m above ground by the readme's rule); the data paper says 3 - 9 m, so points 13 and 14 (11 m) disagree.
The thermistor reads a SCALAR speed and the cup anemometer a 10-minute mean: a RANS |U| is biased low against both.

The files do not say whether a wind direction names where the wind comes from. The cleaned tables read it as the direction the wind comes from (N = 0, E = 90). At NNW a solved field supports that reading: Eddy3D's OpenFOAM 12 run for the wind from NNW correlates R 0.935 with the tunnel's 9 m column labelled NNW and R 0.077 with its column labelled SSE, the opposite wind (clean/QUESTIONS.md QF9); the other directions are not solved and stay unverified.
